prompt: Go to https://www.selenium.dev/selenium/web/web-form.html, fill in the form with some sample data, and submit it.

input.value: This is some sample text for the textarea field.

input.script: (() => { const c = document.querySelector('input[name="my-colors"]'); const r = document.querySelector('input[name="my-range"]'); return JSON.stringify({color: c && c.value, range: r && r.value}); })()

says.text: Now the checkbox, radio, date, and other fields.
Most fields are filled in. The date picker popup is still open. Next I'll set the color picker and the range slider, which can't be typed into.
The color is now #2e86de and the slider is at 8. Submitting the form.

I filled in the form and submitted it. The confirmation page loaded with the heading **"Form submitted"** and the message **"Received!"**

| Field | Value submitted |
|---|---|
| Text input | John Doe |
| Password | SamplePass123 |
| Textarea | This is some sample text for the textarea field. |
| Dropdown (select) | Two |
| Dropdown (datalist) | New York |
| Checkboxes | Both checked |
| Radio | "Default radio" selected |
| Color picker | #2e86de |
| Date picker | 10/29/2026 |
| Range slider | 8 |

- **Skipped fields:** I left the disabled and read-only fields as they were, and didn't upload a file, so the file field went through empty.
- **Color and slider:** these can't be typed into, so I set them with a short script on the page.
- **Password in the URL:** the form sends its data in the address of the confirmation page, so the password appears there as plain text. It's only sample data here, but don't enter a real password on this test page.

I've released control of the browser, and it's still open on the confirmation page.
